doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing Bird and Diz, and music as his life
summary: Hearing Parker and Gillespie changed his playing; he reflects on his age, practice and love of music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I always wanted — it was something I wanted to learn. I almost had a nervous breakdown the first time I heard Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie. It was something so new to me, something I was looking for all my life. Because I had all this technique and didn’t know what to do with it. And my idols were Roy Eldridge and Lester Young. They played so pretty and simple. And I had all this technique. So I gave up playing vibes and playing drums. When I heard Bird and Diz I said what is that? Because they played all these technique things, and I was in the Army at that time. And I listened for fifteen— I

went back and played four million notes, maybe three were right. Maybe. But I knew the timing. I got the timing down. That was my whole life. Music has always been my whole life. So, Monk, seriously, I don’t even buy anything. I’m 76 years old now, with the body of a man 75, so, and the brain of a 19 year old idiot. If I didn’t like music — I am not a millionaire, but I’m okay. I don’t have to go anywhere anymore. I lucked out with land and all that. But the point I’m getting at is if I was in a band that didn’t have fun coming out and playing, I wouldn’t come out. I love sitting at home. By the way, whatever I do I do hard. I get on stage and I play hard. If I sit at home, I do nothing hard. I can do it better than anybody. I can be a couch potato better than anybody living. The hardest part about going out, not as much as I used to, I only go out about four times a month maybe. You’ve got to practice every day. And it’s hard at my age to really get yourself up there and practice. Like George Foreman, 50 years old, if he has to have a fight, you think he wants to run ten miles? No way. He doesn’t want to run around half a block. But to keep in shape and be capable of doing what I’m capable of doing, I’ve got to practice.
